finding.claim: _validate_sub returns early when the sub claim is absent, so a subject= check passes for sub-less tokens (fail-open, unlike iss and aud).
finding.source: Caller passes subject="alice" to jwt.decode; attacker holds a validly signed token from the same key that has no sub claim.
finding.sink: Subject-based authorization in the calling application.

trace.note: decode() forwards subject to decode_complete.
decode_complete passes subject into _validate_claims.
_validate_claims calls _validate_sub when verify_sub is enabled.
Returns early when 'sub' is absent, so the subject comparison at 452-454 never runs.

finding.guards_checked: Signature is verified first (api_jwt.py:267-273, api_jws.py:277-285), so the token must be validly signed. require=['sub'] would block it but is not default. iss and aud raise on missing claims (api_jwt.py:571-572, 529-532), which makes this inconsistent. Conditional severity: medium.

finding.claim: An unknown or missing kid forces a synchronous, unthrottled JWKS refetch before any signature check, with no negative caching.
finding.source: Unauthenticated request carrying a JWT with a random or absent kid header.
finding.sink: Outbound HTTP request to the JWKS endpoint (30s default timeout) inside the request path.

trace.note: get_signing_key_from_jwt reads the header with verification disabled.
Calls get_signing_key(kid).
Cache lookup finds no matching kid.
Calls get_signing_keys(refresh=True), which calls fetch_data.
fetch_data performs urlopen with no rate limit or negative cache.

finding.guards_checked: kid must be a string (api_jws.py:446-448). URI scheme check (jwks_client.py:77-82) does not apply because the URI is developer-supplied. Nothing limits refresh frequency. Severity low to medium (amplification and worker-blocking DoS).

finding.claim: With cache_keys=True, kid-to-key entries are cached indefinitely, so a key removed from the JWKS (revoked) keeps verifying tokens until LRU eviction.
finding.source: Application sets cache_keys=True; a signing key is later removed from the JWKS; attacker presents a token signed with that key.
finding.sink: Signature verification against a revoked key.

trace.note: lru_cache wraps self.get_signing_key with maxsize=max_cached_keys and assigns it to the instance attribute.
get_signing_key_from_jwt calls self.get_signing_key, which resolves to the cached wrapper.
On a cache hit the JWKS is never consulted, so the 5-minute lifespan and refresh do not apply.

finding.guards_checked: Documented in the docstring (jwks_client.py:44-47) as no time-based expiration. Opt-in (cache_keys defaults to False). Exceptions are not cached, so attackers cannot poison the cache. Severity low to medium.

finding.claim: PyJWK exception messages embed the full JWK dict, including private parameters (d, p, q, dp, dq, qi) and HMAC secret k, which violates the org no-sensitive-logging policy when exceptions are logged.
finding.source: A malformed or unsupported private JWK (missing kty, missing crv, or unknown alg) is passed to PyJWK directly.
finding.sink: Exception text that the application may log or return.

trace.note: Reads kty from the JWK data.
Raises f'kty is not found: {self._jwk_data}', embedding the full dict.
Same pattern for a missing crv on OKP keys.
Same pattern for an unknown alg, raising PyJWKError with the full dict.

finding.guards_checked: PyJWKSet swallows these errors (api_jwk.py:152-157), so exposure is limited to direct PyJWK construction. No redaction is applied. Severity low to medium.

finding.claim: HMAC prepare_key rejects PEM and SSH key forms but accepts DER-encoded asymmetric public keys as an HMAC secret, enabling algorithm confusion when an application passes raw DER and allows HS*.
finding.source: Application passes DER bytes of an RSA or EC public key as the verification key with algorithms including HS256; the attacker knows the public key.
finding.sink: HMAC verification using the public key bytes as the secret.

trace.note: is_pem_format and is_ssh_key reject only PEM and SSH forms.
json.loads on DER bytes raises ValueError or UnicodeError, which is caught, so the JWK check does not reject.
prepare_key returns the DER bytes as the HMAC secret.

finding.guards_checked: PEM and SSH and JWK-shaped checks block the common confusion path. RSAAlgorithm.prepare_key rejects DER with InvalidKeyError, so only HS* is affected. Docstring warns against mixing HS and RS. Requires developer misconfiguration. Severity low.

finding.claim: Attacker-controlled kid is interpolated unescaped into PyJWKClientError text, allowing log injection via embedded newlines or control characters.
finding.source: JWT header with a kid containing a newline (JSON escape) or other control characters.
finding.sink: Application logs of the exception message.

trace.note: kid is read from the unverified header; only the str type is validated (api_jws.py:446-448).
No match found after refresh.
Raises f'Unable to find a signing key that matches: "{kid}"' with no escaping.

finding.guards_checked: Only str type is validated; control characters are not filtered. Severity low.
